title: Where to start
author: Original-Yak658
selftext:
Hi all, firstly I just want to say this is a great change to the usual AI is evil and will kill us all. I mean maybe it will kill us, but that's just a deep rooted fear of watching The Terminator when I was 6.

I have made a couple of small mobile games using chatGPT, but want to start working on something larger.

So my question to you is what do you use? I see a lot of Claude, but don't even know where to begin with anything beyond chatGPT.

Any additional information on why you use the AI of your choice, how much it costs and the kind of results you have gotten will all be appreciated. 

Once again, a huge thank you to all of you for building a great and supportive community.

comments.author: Several-Mess2288
comments.body: I started with claude a week ago. If you didnt use something similar to claude code where he can handle the project locally, go try it, not gonna regret. And before starting check out how to use it efficiently. it costs 20 dollars. I would show my results but I heard people can copy games with ai

comments.author: DreamBigGamesReddit
comments.body:
This sub has started getting this question a lot. A few simple games were made and the OP has a question about scaling. The best answer that’s been given is to ask your model of choice to help you with that.

Ask it to plan a game with you, design documents, file structuring, concept art, references, git commits, etc.

Instead of asking us this question, go ask your model’s chatbot these same questions and build your workflow around its output.

Remember, if it makes sense to you and it’s making progress, it’s correct. There are a million ways to be correct with this.

comments.author: standardofiron
comments.body:
Pasting my other comment; Here I explain the workflow I use with Claude Code (but it should work with other CLI tools too), Blender, and Godot to quickly get a 3D game up and running: https://youtu.be/ONoyH2TpSl8

This is also the approach I’m using with my kids, and I honestly think it’s one of the simplest and most fun ways to start getting into game development with AI.

comments.author: JDad67
comments.body:
Here is my process once I know the game I am aiming for. 

1. Figure out what assets I am going to use. Asset pack? Procedurally generated? AI generated? 

2. Start a chat with Fable-level agent (or opus 5.5 which ever) asking it to make a comprehensive planning document based on my description of the game, and the assets I want to use. If I know the tech stack I want I specify it otherwise I just tell it the platform(s) I want to run on. I specify that I want the agents to work autonomously but give it permission to ask questions earlier than later. Test over assume. 

This is usually a 30 minute discussion of questions and answers. Ask if you are unsure of anything. Push back on anything you don’t like.  

3. I review the output document. Create a folder on my Mac, start an opus coding agent. Drop the planning document into it telling it to ask questions as needed. 

4. If I am having it generate assets that’s usually a separate pipeline and I have it set up a feedback queue where I can approve reject assets as needed.
